name: Skin Care Routine Checklist
description: A step-by-step morning and evening skincare routine, with simple notes to adapt it to your skin type.

items.text: Cleanse with a gentle face wash to remove overnight oil
Apply any morning treatment or antioxidant serum
items.note: Vitamin C is a common morning option; introduce actives slowly.

items.text: Apply moisturizer suited to your skin type
Finish with broad-spectrum sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher
items.note: Sunscreen always goes on as the last skincare step in the morning.

items.text: Let each layer absorb for a moment before the next
Reapply sunscreen during the day if outdoors a lot
Remove makeup and sunscreen before cleansing
Cleanse to wash away the day's dirt, oil and pollution
Apply any night treatment such as a retinoid, as directed
items.note: Start a couple of nights a week and build up to avoid irritation.

items.text: Apply a moisturizer, slightly richer than your daytime one
Add eye cream or facial oil last if you use them
Skip sunscreen at night; it is only needed by day
Use lukewarm water rather than hot, which can dry skin
Choose a gentle, non-stripping cleanser
Massage cleanser in for around 30 seconds
Pat your face dry with a clean towel instead of rubbing
Avoid harsh scrubbing, which can irritate and inflame skin
items.note: Limit physical exfoliation to once or twice a week if you use it.

items.text: Oily skin: pick lightweight, oil-free or gel moisturizers
Dry skin: use a richer cream and look for hydrating ingredients
Combination skin: balance lighter and richer products by area
Sensitive skin: choose fragrance-free, gentle formulas
items.note: Patch test new products and add them one at a time.

items.text: All types: still cleanse, moisturize and wear sunscreen daily
Patch test new products before using them on your face
Introduce one active ingredient at a time
Drink water and aim for regular, restful sleep
Wash pillowcases and clean phone screens regularly
Avoid picking or popping spots, which can scar
Important: this is general information, not medical advice
items.note: See a dermatologist for persistent or worsening skin concerns.

faq.q: What order should I apply skincare products?
faq.a: A simple rule is thinnest to thickest. In the morning: cleanse, apply any treatment or serum, moisturize, then finish with sunscreen. At night, swap sunscreen for a slightly richer moisturizer and use treatments as directed.

faq.q: Do I really need sunscreen every day?
faq.a: Yes. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher is one of the most effective steps for protecting skin from sun damage and premature aging, even on cloudy days and when indoors near windows.

faq.q: How do I adjust the routine for my skin type?
faq.a: Choose a gentle cleanser for all types, a lighter moisturizer for oily skin and a richer one for dry skin, and fragrance-free products for sensitive skin. Introduce active ingredients slowly and patch test new products first.

faq.q: Can I print this skin care routine checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off your cleanse, treat, moisturize and SPF steps each morning and night to keep your routine consistent.
No. This is general information about everyday skincare, not medical advice. See a dermatologist for persistent acne, rashes, changing moles or any skin concern that does not improve.
